newsitem.title: UK: EARLY LME ACTIVITY SUBDUED, STOCKS FAIL TO IMPACT.
newsitem.headline: EARLY LME ACTIVITY SUBDUED, STOCKS FAIL TO IMPACT.

text.p: Trading in base metals got off to a slow start on Monday, a condition that was likely to continue until later ring trading.
The release of London Metal Exchange (LME) stocks data failed to spark any movement as they were viewed as neutral.
"The stocks came in much as expected," one trader commented. Copper quietly traded below $2,300 a tonne, while zinc continued to find support from tight nearby backwardations.

Three months delivery copper was last at $2,297, a $9 gain from Friday's LME kerb close. Traders said copper was capped at around $2,300 following another inventory rise and several suggested prices could test support at $2,270 following a downtrending chart close on Friday.
A stocks fall of 1,125 tonnes helped lift zinc by $3 to $1,550.
Traders said the market continued to find strong underlying support from nearby backwardations which were showing few signs of easing.

Despite a warning by the LME on Thursday about players with dominant positions pushing prices higher, zinc's cash to three months backwardation was indicated at a $160/$170 backwardation, versus $155 on Friday.
Traders said the market remained physically tight amid concern over Chinese smelters which last year sold forward at low prices as much as 250,000 tonnes. Most of the positions mature in September.
Aluminium drifted back by $6 to $1,740. Traders said the move came against the backdrop of a recently over-extended market. Traders pegged support at $1,710, $1,700 and $1,680.
Elsewhere, nickel moved lower under trade selling to straddle $7,000. On Friday it closed at $7,085.
Tin drifted to be indicated last at $5,560/80, against $5,605, while lead was unchanged at $614.
